description: Machine-readable registry of CI-pinned documentation behavior claims (the claims-fixture gate, ADR-0023). Each claim states exactly what its named engine test pins - no more. The claim's normative sentence must appear on one of its pages (check 8 of scripts/check-doc-canon.py: whitespace-normalized, case-insensitive containment) and the engine test pin must exist and pass in the normal build. Origin: the AI grammar coverage study found all documentation drift in ungated prose - this gate extends drift testing from shape to behavior. An AI agent may treat these claims as source-verified.

claims.claim: The flow exception context exposes the HTTP status under error.code.
claims.quote: error.code - the status code of the exception

claims.claim: When application.properties and application.yml define the same key, the .yml value wins (application.yml is merged last).
claims.quote: `application.yml` is merged last

claims.claim: The Kafka flow adapter treats any flow reply status below 400 (2xx/3xx) as success - acknowledged, never retried or dead-lettered.
claims.quote: A flow **succeeds** when it replies with a status below `400`

claims.claim: Registering a duplicate route does not fail the application: the earlier registration is reloaded and the newest function serves.
claims.quote: a duplicate route reloads the earlier registration

claims.claim: @PreLoad envInstances names a configuration KEY looked up in application.properties; a nonexistent key falls back to the annotation's instances.
claims.quote: envInstances names a property key looked up in

claims.claim: A flows.yaml manifest that omits 'location' loads its flow files from classpath:/flows/.
claims.quote: Default: `classpath:/flows/`

claims.claim: A non-boolean, non-numeric decision value coerces to 1 and silently selects the first branch.
claims.quote: silently select the first branch

claims.claim: The Playground inspect command resolves whole subtrees, not only leaf keys.
claims.quote: `inspect` returns subtrees too

claims.claim: Graph export does not reject orphan nodes; the CompileGraph deployment gate re-validates the whole model.
claims.quote: Orphan nodes are not rejected at export

claims.claim: The reserved model-metadata key set is exactly ten names: cid, instance, flow, ttl, trace, parent, root, none, run, iteration_index.
claims.quote:
`model.parent`, `model.root`, `model.none`, `model.run`,
  `model.iteration_index`

claims.claim: rest.yaml's stream: true is parsed by the engine and streaming replies ride a dedicated ordered reply lane.
claims.quote: progressive response streaming (SSE / chunked JSON Lines) on a dedicated ordered reply lane

claims.claim: In a MiniGraph data mapping a source that resolves to null (a missing key, or a plugin returning null) clears a model.* target (removed, or set to null when the source key exists or the target is indexed) and leaves any other target untouched - the same rule as Event Script - so a default for a model variable must come from the source side, never from default-then-overlay.
claims.quote: A null source clears a `model.*` target and leaves any other target untouched

claims.claim: In graph.math a boolean is never a number: a boolean operand in arithmetic, in a </> comparison or as a function argument - and a COMPUTE whose result is a bare boolean - fails naming the selector instead of computing as 1 or 0; an unknown function, an overflow to infinity and a division by zero fail by name too.
claims.quote: each enforced by a named failure rather than a silent value

claims.claim: Closing a Kafka flow consumer makes its member leave the consumer group immediately (LeaveGroup), so its partitions are reassigned at once rather than after the session timeout; the adapter closes every binding's consumer on JVM shutdown through the platform shutdown lifecycle.
claims.quote: the consumer's close sends the group coordinator a **LeaveGroup**: the member's partitions are reassigned to the surviving members at once

claims.claim: On shutdown the shared Kafka producer is closed after the consumers, waiting at most the ten-second grace for buffered records to be acknowledged; records still unacknowledged when the grace ends are failed and counted in the log rather than waited for.
claims.quote: waiting up to the same ten seconds for its buffered records to be acknowledged

claims.claim: graph.model.automation accepts a comma-separated list of graph manifests, each with its own location; when two manifests list the same graph id, the later manifest wins - its copy replaces the earlier one, and a rejected later copy leaves the id not executable (404).
claims.quote: accepts a comma-separated list of manifests, each carrying its own location, and when two manifests list the same graph id the later manifest wins

claims.claim: A deployment manifest's sets register all of a set's graphs or none: when one graph of a set fails the gate, no graph of that set is executable.
claims.quote: a set registers all of its graphs or none

claims.claim: A duplicate graph id that involves a packaged set is logged as an ERROR, and the later copy in compile order owns the id.
claims.quote: a duplicate that involves a set is logged as an ERROR

claims.claim: sets need an unpack folder of their own: a file:/ location the application can write; a classpath: value, the Playground temp folder, a folder another manifest uses, or no unpack at all skips the manifest's sets with an ERROR while its loose graphs still compile.
claims.quote: `sets` need a writable `unpack` folder of their own

claims.claim: A set whose entry is not named <graph-id>.json with a valid id is rejected before any file is written to the unpack folder.
claims.quote: rejected before any file is written

claims.claim: The generated manifest in the unpack folder records every file the loader wrote, and the next start removes the file of a graph a new version of the set no longer holds; no other file is touched.
claims.quote: the next start removes a graph a new version of the set no longer holds

claims.claim: The graph.math expression dialect is exactly: number, string and boolean literals; the operators ** (right-associative; a unary operand needs parentheses), unary + - !, * / %, + - (+ concatenates when either side is a string), < <= > >= (two numbers, or two strings compared lexically), == != (same type only, except that a string that is a canonical number compares as a number in all six comparison operators), && || (short-circuit), the ternary ?: and parentheses; the eighteen built-in functions sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, sqrt, abs, floor, ceil, round, log, log10, exp, min, max, pow, random (each also under Math.); and the constants PI and E. Nothing else parses: no bitwise operators, no assignment or user variables, no user-defined functions - an unlisted function fails by name.
claims.quote: This list is the whole dialect: an operator, function or constant not listed here is rejected by name, never silently accepted.

claims.claim: A graph.math DECIMAL statement is the high-precision COMPUTE: the expression is evaluated with exact decimal arithmetic and the result is stored as a canonical decimal string (plain notation, the computed scale kept, a zero of any scale written "0"); a Double or Float value is converted through its shortest decimal text at its minimal scale (exact over that text, and only as exact as the computation that produced it); rounding is always explicit, round(x, scale, mode); sqrt, log, log10, exp, trigonometry, random() and the constants PI and E are refused by name; COMPUTE is unchanged.
claims.quote: `DECIMAL` is the high-precision `COMPUTE`: exact decimal arithmetic whose result is a canonical decimal string, and `COMPUTE` is untouched.

claims.claim: In graph.math a string that is a canonical number (plain notation: an optional minus sign, digits without leading zeros, an optional fraction) compares as a number in == != < <= > >=, so '200' == '200', 200 == 200 and 200 == '200' are the same comparison and '9.5' < '10.25' compares 9.5 with 10.25; the comparison is exact, and text that is not a canonical number keeps the strict rules.
claims.quote: A string that is a canonical number compares as a number

claims.claim: In a graph.math DECIMAL statement a JSON number (a Double or Float) is accepted and converted through the shortest decimal text it prints as, at its minimal scale and in plain notation (5.0E-4 is 0.0005, 100.0 is 100), so a number and the same decimal written as a string give the same answer; it is exact over that text and only as exact as the computation that produced the number, which the guide declares so that sending numbers instead of strings is a conscious decision.
claims.quote: A JSON number is a double, and `DECIMAL` converts it through the shortest decimal text it prints as, at its minimal scale

claims.claim: In a MiniGraph data mapping a {namespace.key} reference inside a source resolves before the source is read - as a key segment (table.{model.key}), a list index (items[{model.i}]) or text in a constant or a plugin argument - and its value is inserted verbatim: a '!', '>', '&&' or '==' in a text constant does not quote it, and only a JSONPath filter quotes a text value; an unresolved reference renders the text null, so a composed key misses and the null-source rule applies; a composed key is case-sensitive.
claims.quote: A `{namespace.key}` reference inside a mapping source resolves before the source is read, and its value is inserted verbatim, never quoted

claims.claim: A $. JSONPath mapping source takes Jayway's result shape - by the kind of path, not the number of matches: a definite path (child member names and single indexes only) yields the value, or null when it is absent; an indefinite path (a filter, a wildcard, a deep scan, a slice or a union) always yields a list, one match being a one-element list and no match an empty list, unless a member name before its first indefinite step is missing, which yields null.
claims.quote: The result shape depends on the kind of path, not on the number of matches

claims.claim: A MsgPack payload the engine decodes - an event envelope, an Event API request, MsgPack.unpack - may nest at most 64 maps and lists, the outermost container being level 1, so an envelope's body may nest 63; one level more is refused as a decoding error naming the limit (Nesting deeper than 64 levels; HTTP 400 at the Event API) before the decoder's recursion can exhaust the stack.
claims.quote: A payload nested deeper than 64 maps and lists is refused as a decoding error, the envelope map being level 1

claims.claim: A MsgPack decoder of the engine - MsgPack.unpack, the path the Event API feeds, the envelope and CanonicalPackager.decode - checks a declared str, bin or ext length and a declared array or map count against the bytes that remain before anything is allocated or consumed, so a header that promises more than the input holds is refused at the header as a decoding error, never as an unchecked exception or an allocation sized by the header, and the format byte 0xc1, which the specification never uses, is refused; the shared vector file msgpack-hostile-header-vectors.json pins the same inputs in both engines.
claims.quote: A header that promises more than the input holds is refused at the header

claims.claim: Empty MsgPack input decodes as an empty map at MsgPack.unpack, so an empty byte array is an empty envelope and never a decoding error, while CanonicalPackager.decode refuses empty input because a package is never empty; this engine is the reference implementation the Rust engine follows, and the shared vector file pins the case as the control the event codec accepts and the canonical decoder rejects.
claims.quote: Empty input decodes as an empty map, so an empty byte array is an empty envelope and never a decoding error

claims.claim: A MsgPack payload the engine decodes holds exactly one value: MsgPack.unpack, the path the Event API feeds, the envelope and CanonicalPackager.decode refuse bytes after the top-level container, well-formed or not, as a decoding error (Unexpected bytes after the value at offset N; IllegalArgumentException at EventEnvelope; HTTP 400 at the Event API), so two different byte strings never decode to the same value; the canonical decoder always did, the event codec does since this change, and the shared vector file pins an empty map followed by 0xc1 and by a well-formed nil in both engines.
claims.quote: Bytes after the top-level container, well-formed or not, are refused as a decoding error
